requirements.requirement: Create an opsbot account on node1
requirements.summary: Confirmed opsbot did not exist prior (cmd-b4ca6e88fdca4080), then created with useradd -m and locked password via passwd -l, id opsbot shows uid=1000(opsbot) (cmd-c00e1b18008b40e3). Directly observed on node1.

requirements.requirement: opsbot account exists on node2 (needed for key-based access target)
requirements.summary: Confirmed opsbot absent (cmd-96812d9d81154ca3), then created with useradd -m and locked password (cmd-aaf7c9385c604bf6), id opsbot shows uid=1000(opsbot) on node2.

requirements.requirement: opsbot on node1 has SSH key-based access to run commands as opsbot on node2
requirements.summary: Generated ed25519 keypair for opsbot on node1 (cmd-59b752eb35f6449d), retrieved pubkey (cmd-ee99fa84f0b64441), installed it into node2's opsbot authorized_keys with correct ownership/perms (cmd-7b10b9231f614717), and directly observed a successful key-only SSH command execution (`whoami` returning `opsbot`, exit 0, BatchMode=yes) from node1 to node2 (cmd-75fff379b8304aff). An earlier attempt failed due to missing host keys on node2 (cmd-f042d60318e341be) but was a transient discovery step corrected before the final successful run.

requirements.requirement: Require key-based authentication for opsbot on both systems (password authentication rejected)
requirements.summary: Baseline sshd_config.d/60-cloudimg-settings.conf already set PasswordAuthentication no globally on both nodes (cmd-13da46b482a94e83, cmd-bfe8801c07174006). Executor additionally added an explicit Match User opsbot block (PubkeyAuthentication yes, PasswordAuthentication no, AuthenticationMethods publickey) confirmed present after config write and reload (cmd-8af45c75ab4445e7, cmd-739630e5f367455b). Directly observed password-only SSH attempts to opsbot rejected with 'Permission denied (publickey)' on node1 (cmd-4c75fe1e9bbc43e9) and node2 (cmd-66ab01fc80db4bc9).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node with pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: For node1: healthy baseline (boot_id 1e0cb179..., ssh.socket active, opsbot present) captured in cmd-fbf150010a7f4f47, matching the fixed before/after-prepare snapshot. Reboot issued and acknowledged via connection reset (cmd-b65a6f2c298c4808), new boot_id 37dd6d9c... confirmed (cmd-9cab9be30b6f4d7d), matching the after-executor snapshot, and recovery of ssh.socket, opsbot account/keys, sshd Match block, and working key-based SSH to node2 verified (cmd-8af45c75ab4445e7). For node2: identical pattern with baseline boot_id 29011044... (cmd-9b8a8c357b834ffd), reboot ack (cmd-834b9aaaa99b4be9), new boot_id 8612462b... (cmd-ef418152abf3407e) matching after-executor snapshot, and recovery of account/keys/config confirmed (cmd-739630e5f367455b), plus a post-reboot cross-node SSH success (cmd-cba3e28c8ab447d3) and password-rejection re-check (cmd-7e820c95a378426b). Fixed lifecycle boot-identity observations independently corroborate both transitions.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the public task contract are directly satisfied: an opsbot account exists on both node1 and node2, opsbot on node1 has demonstrated key-based SSH command execution against opsbot on node2, and password authentication for opsbot is confirmed rejected on both systems via observed 'Permission denied (publickey)' results. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also fully and coherently executed and cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots for both nodes, showing healthy baseline, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity, and full recovery of the opsbot configuration and cross-node SSH access. Operational hygiene is high with no unnecessary or unreverted mutations identified.
limitations: The initial sshd -t failures due to missing host keys (return_code 255 on cmd-fa62d11e5f6943d9/cmd-69ad5474315e4654) reveal the base image shipped without SSH host keys; this was a pre-existing image condition rather than an executor-caused fault, and was resolved before the final SSH verification.

The captured evidence for password-rejection checks uses PreferredAuthentications=password with PubkeyAuthentication=no rather than fully interactive password prompts, but this is an accepted standard way to test that pubkey-only auth is enforced without needing an actual password.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all 43 terminal commands chronologically. All state-changing actions trace to a clear purpose: account creation, keypair generation (with a corrective chown after an initial permission-denied attempt), authorized_keys installation, sshd Match-block config writes, missing host-key generation (ssh-keygen -A, required since the fresh image lacked host keys), creation of the missing /run/sshd privilege-separation directory, ssh.socket restarts to apply config, and the two mandated node reboots. No unnecessary, abandoned, or destructive mutations were found; failed commands (e.g. cmd-296b95967f7d465d, cmd-e7f2ddede9a24426, cmd-4630ff97060e4795, cmd-fa62d11e5f6943d9, cmd-f042d60318e341be) were either read-only discovery or corrected troubleshooting steps that left no residue and were followed by successful corrective actions. No security controls were weakened; the added Match block only tightens auth for opsbot.
